newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Spanish, Moroccan bank merger not approved yet.
newsitem.headline: Spanish, Moroccan bank merger not approved yet.

text.p: Spanish Uniban bank expects its merger with Morocco's leading Wafabank to be approved by main shareholders by end January or early February, a Uniban senior manager said on Thursday.

"Only an extraordinary general assembly attended by major shareholder has the power to approve the merger...Its meeting will take place by end January or beginning of February," the official told Reuters by telephone.
Uniban held an ordinary general assembly on Thursday but did not examine the merger issue, he said but gave no other details.
The meeting, which was initially scheduled for December 30, 1996, was delayed then for "technical reasons", a bank spokesman said earlier.
Wafabank decided to buy 100 percent of Uniban or more than 2.46 million shares priced at around $28 million, a bourse official said.
A Casablanca-based stockbroker said: "The dispute between a group of shareholders over the shares parity and the management was apparently behind the delay in the approval of the merger."
Wafabank is offering one share in exchange for five shares of Uniban while shareholders wanted one share against four, the broker added.
Uniban registered a net profit of 0.6 million dirhams in the first half of this year from losses of 27.2 million dirhams in the whole period of 1995. No further figures have yet been released.
The effective absorption of Uniban by Wafabank will take place by end March 1997, a Wafabank official said earlier.

Fuelled by the rumours of the merger, Wafabank shares were in demand on the market and rose over the line of 500 dirhams in recent weeks. The stock was traded at 597 dirhams on Thursday, up 17 dirhams over the previous session.
